title: Lasso: Accurate and Efficient Detection of Long-Lived Sparse Items in High-Speed Data Streams

problem.claim: Detecting long-lived sparse items in high-speed data streams is important because they may indicate stealthy or low-rate threats.

gap.claim: Existing approaches trade off lookup accuracy or update efficiency and overlook deployability under practical hardware constraints.

contributions.claim: Lasso is a lightweight, hardware-conscious approach for detecting long-lived sparse items under tight memory and throughput constraints.
Lasso prioritizes candidates using persistence-frequency deviations and protects long-lived items with fine-grained temporal awareness.
The authors develop a formal analytical model for Lasso.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report high detection accuracy and processing throughput under tight memory budgets on Tofino-1 programmable switches and FPGA platforms.
The authors report that extensive evaluations on CPU, Tofino, and FPGA platforms demonstrate high accuracy and throughput within strict resource constraints.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-lived sparse items matter for identifying possible stealthy or low-rate threats in high-speed streams.
Prior methods have accuracy, update-cost, and deployability limitations under constrained processing substrates.
Lasso combines hardware-conscious detection, persistence-frequency deviation handling, and temporally aware protection.
A formal analytical model is provided to establish the approach's theoretical soundness.
Evaluations across CPU, Tofino, and FPGA platforms report accuracy and throughput under strict resource constraints.

source_observation.claim: Long-lived sparse items are described as having a small gap between persistence and frequency.

interpretation.claim: A detector can prioritize candidates by identifying items whose persistence and frequency remain closely aligned.

application.claim: Use persistence-frequency deviation as a candidate-ranking signal in streaming anomaly or threat detection.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this signal generalizes beyond the studied item-detection setting.

source_observation.claim: Abundant short-lived items can prematurely displace long-lived items in highly skewed streams.

interpretation.claim: Temporal protection may be needed when stream skew causes frequent short-lived items to dominate resource allocation.

application.claim: In skewed streaming workloads, add temporally aware protection for candidates expected to persist.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the skew conditions or protection policy under which this approach is effective.

unknowns: Specific datasets, workloads, and threat scenarios are not provided.
Accuracy and throughput metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
Algorithmic parameters, memory usage, and update costs are not specified.
The formal model's assumptions and conclusions are not described.
Hardware configurations and evaluation conditions are not specified.
